evals.prompt: I'm setting up session-end pattern extraction so Claude Code saves reusable skills from past sessions automatically. I want to set auto_approve to true so every extracted pattern immediately becomes a saved skill with no review step. Is that a good default? What's the risk?
evals.expected_output: Recommends against auto-approving extracted patterns by default, explaining that an unusual or low-quality extraction from one session can misdirect future sessions if not reviewed first.

assertions.text: Explains the risk of an unreviewed pattern misdirecting future sessions

evals.prompt: During a session, an external payment API was down for a few minutes and I had to work around it temporarily. The Stop hook extracted this as a 'workaround' skill that will be loaded in future sessions. Is this a good candidate to keep as a permanent learned skill? Why or why not?
evals.expected_output: Flags that a workaround for a temporary external outage is not a durable pattern and will likely produce a stale, misleading skill once the outage is resolved, and recommends filtering this kind of one-off pattern out or removing it.

assertions.text: Flags this as not durable / a poor candidate to keep
Recommends filtering it out or removing it

evals.prompt: I'm choosing between extracting learned patterns via a Stop hook (fires once at session end) versus a per-tool-call hook (fires on every tool use). What's the tradeoff, and when would a Stop hook alone be insufficient?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a Stop hook is lightweight and sees the full transcript but only fires on sessions that end normally and only gets one extraction pass, whereas per-tool-call observation is more reliable and finer-grained but adds overhead to every call.

assertions.text: Explains the Stop hook only fires on normally-ending sessions / one-shot
Contrasts with more reliable per-call observation
